subject: Checkoutly: sudden p95 latency increase - mitigation & customer update
messages:
From: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@checkoutly.com>
To: markus_klein@redwood.com
Cc: sara.li@checkoutly.com
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Checkoutly: sudden p95 latency increase - mitigation & customer update

Markus —

Heads up: starting ~07:45 PT we saw a jump in API p95 for our checkout scoring endpoints from ~180ms to ~1.2s. This is across both gen and embed calls and is affecting checkout throughput for ~10% of requests. Attached is a short perf capture from our side (incident_snapshot.png).

Can Redwood flip any routing or fallback quickly? We need something that reduces tail latency while we investigate root cause — even a temporary model fallback or routing to a different region is fine. Our SLO is 500ms p95, and we're passing that threshold for a meaningful portion of traffic.

Appreciate a quick proposed plan and ETA.

— Tom
VP Engineering, Checkoutly

---
Incident details (from our logs):
- spike started 2026-06-15T14:45Z
- affected model: redwood-gen-alpha-1 (v202605)
- error rate: unchanged
- QPS: steady; increased median token length for some sessions
From: markus_klein@redwood.com
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, soojin_lee@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 08:28:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Checkoutly: sudden p95 latency increase - mitigation & customer update

Team — forwarding Checkoutly report. Key ask: temporary mitigation to bring p95 under 500ms ASAP, plus an internal plan so we can give a clear ETA back to Tom. Please reply with concrete steps and who owns them.

Suggested options to consider (short-term):
- route Checkoutly traffic to a lower-capacity but lower-tail model variant (redwood-gen-alpha-1-quant)
- enable prefix/KV warm cache for known session prefixes (fast path)
- reduce max_tokens for streaming calls for 30m window
- move a % of traffic to a different availability region if cross-region latency is acceptable

Ben — can you assess routing + kernel-side options?
Marissa — can you confirm if we can open a temporary dedicated slot / reserved pool for them?
Soojin — if this is a KV warmup/story, can the runtime team push a cache prewarm?

I will draft a short customer-facing update once we lock the triage plan.

Thanks,
Markus
Head of Product Operations
From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: markus_klein@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, soojin_lee@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Checkoutly: sudden p95 latency increase - mitigation & customer update

Quick triage notes — I've started a parallel check of the routing table and kernel scheduling logs. Early signals:
- A small subset of gen instances (~6%) are showing tokenization and attention kernel slowdowns on redwood-gen-alpha-1 (v202605) during long sequences (>1024 tokens).
- No increase in 5xxs; throttles are not currently being hit.

Short-term remediation I can execute in the next 15–30 mins:
1) Push routing policy override for Checkoutly service-id -> route 60% traffic to redwood-gen-alpha-1-quant (quantized variant) which has lower tail on long-sequence workloads.
2) Force prefix/KV caching on known checkout session prefixes for the next 45 minutes (prewarm cache).
3) Limit streaming max_tokens to 512 for sessions flagged as high-latency for 30 minutes.

Risk/notes: quant variant has slightly different sampling characteristics; we should flag to Checkoutly that responses may be marginally shorter. I will coordinate kernel selection and monitor for immediate regressions.

I'll post updates to the incident channel and can roll back routing in <1m if needed. Assigning ownership: routing override — Ben; cache prewarm — Soojin; reserved slot request — Marissa (if needed).

— Ben
Senior SRE
From: soojin_lee@redwood.com
To: markus_klein@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 09:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Checkoutly: sudden p95 latency increase - mitigation & customer update

Markus / Ben — cache prewarm in progress. Plan details:
- Prewarm targets: session prefixes seen in Checkoutly logs (we've pulled the top 50 prefixes)
- Estimated warmup time: ~8 minutes to fill hot-KV and stabilize tail for affected instances
- Metrics to watch: kv_warm_hit_rate, gen_token_lat_p95 by instance

Also: asking runtime to apply a transient conservative kernel selector for long sequences to avoid the slow attention path — this is low-risk and reversible. If Ben pushes the routing override, I'll coordinate the cache affinity so caches are warmed on the nodes receiving the traffic.

I'll update the incident channel when warm hits cross 80%.

— Soojin
Runtime Lead (Serving)
From: markus_klein@redwood.com
To: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@checkoutly.com>, Sara Li <sara.li@checkoutly.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, soojin_lee@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Checkoutly: sudden p95 latency increase - mitigation & customer update

Tom / Sara — quick update from Redwood: thank you for the perf snapshot; we have a short remediation plan in flight and will keep you updated minute-by-minute for the next 45m. Current actions taken: 

1) We have applied a temporary routing override: ~60% of your traffic is on the quantized variant (redwood-gen-alpha-1-quant) to reduce tail latency for long sequences.
2) We are prewarming the KV/prefix cache for your top 50 session prefixes — warm hits are expected to cross 80% within ~10 minutes.
3) We limited streaming max_tokens to 512 for sessions detected as long-running during the mitigation window.

What to expect: p95 should drop toward your 500ms target for the majority of traffic within the next 10–15 minutes. There is a small chance (low) that text length/response shape changes slightly on the quantized path; we will monitor quality and roll traffic back when stable.

We will send another operational note at +30m and a summary post-mortem once we have root cause. If you want immediate rollback to original model for a portion of traffic, tell us the % and we can adjust the override.

Attachments: incident_snapshot.png (your upload), routing-policy-diff.pdf (internal override diff).

Best,
Markus
Head of Product Operations
Redwood Inference
